sections.content: HTML exposes hooks for scripts: ids and classes for selection, data-* attributes for custom data, and semantic elements for behavior (details toggles natively).
The DOM (Document Object Model) is the live tree scripts manipulate — every element becomes a node with properties, methods, and events.
Key points: querySelector('#id') / querySelector('.class') are the main selectors, events (click, input) attach behavior, and innerHTML rebuilds content (careful with injection).
Try this variation — change a value, predict the output, then run it:
sections.codeExample:
<button id="save" data-action="save">Save</button>
<script>
document.getElementById("save").addEventListener("click", () => {
    console.log("saved!");
});
</script>
